main_text.p: Vel Iniquum & Falsum. Exod. XXIII, 7. Prov. XVII, 15. Jef. V,23. Luc.XVI,15.
Ita fit, ut diversimodè capiatur, tum Verbum Justificare, tum Nomen Justificatio.

Hîc, de Justificatione Dei, agere propositum est: Non, quâ Deus justificatur ab hominibus: h. e. Justus agnoscitur & deprædicatur: Psalm. LI, 5. Roman. III, 4. Luc. VII,29. 35.&c. conf. Prov. VIII, 9. cum Matth. XI,19.
Sed, quâ Deus justificat Homines, Judicio ejus oblatos: & velut ad Tribunal Dei constitutos.
Justificatio hominis coram Deo, duplex in Sacris nob. describitur: Legalis una, altera Evangelica.
Illa fundatur, in Lege: Homo ille, qui fecerit præcepta Legis, vivet in iis: Levit. XVIII,5. Rom. II, 13. Gal. III, 12.
Hæc, in Evangelio: Qui crediderit, servabitur. Marc. XVI, 16.
Videatur Apostolus, utramque contendens: Rom. X, 3.—10. & Gal. III, 10.—14. & Phil. III, 9.
Legalis igitur est: quâ Deus Hominem, in semetipso, suisque factis, Justum declarat: atque adeò, cùm à Damnatione absolvit, tum pro illâ justitiâ gratiosè remunerat.

Estque iterum, vel Hominis, respectu Dei, quoad Univer-salem Personæ & operum justitiam, ad rigorem Legis & Juris exactam: Et sic nemo hominum justificatus fuit vel erit: Job. IX, 2. 3. Psal. CXLIII, 2. Rom. III, 9. 10. & seqq. 20. Gal. III, 16. 22. Eph. II, 8. 9. &c.
Unus solus Jesus Christus, Mediator Dei & Hominum, excipitur: Jef. L, 8. & I. Tim. III, 16.
Vel Hominis comparatè ad Hominem, unum vel plures, respectu Particularis alicujus [a] Dicti vel [b] Facti, qualitercunque justi, & Legi Dei conformis.

page.notes: No running head. The faint mirrored text at the edges and the faint word at the lower left are show-through from the other side of the leaf and were left out. No catchword was clearly visible. The brackets around [a] and [b] are printed. The numeral in "I. Tim." is a small, slightly blurred letter and may be a Roman I or 1.
